title: As the Deer
subtitle: Psalms 42–72 in Poems & Pictures
author: Timothy Holt
beforeYouBegin:
Book Two of the Psalter runs from a deer searching a dry creek bed for water to the line that closes it: the prayers of David, son of Jesse, are ended. In between are the songs of a king who hid in caves, sinned and confessed, grew old, and kept praying.

This volume answers them one at a time, thirty-one short poems in four parts, each beside a picture and under a single line from the psalm it answers. It picks up where Planted by the Water left off.

The poems are not the Bible. They are one reader's response to it. Keep the Psalms open alongside this book, and let the real words have the last word.

parts.title: As the Deer
parts.epigraph: As the deer pants for the water brooks, so my soul pants after you, God.
parts.lightHint: Near 'preach to yourself' (Psalm 42:1–5) in Part 1: As the Deer

parts.title: A Clean Heart
parts.epigraph: Create in me a clean heart, O God. Renew a right spirit within me.
parts.lightHint: Near 'a thousand hills' (Psalm 50:10–15) in Part 2: A Clean Heart

parts.title: The Rock Higher Than I
parts.epigraph: My soul rests in God alone.
parts.lightName: Light of The Rock Higher Than I
parts.lightHint: Near 'someone keeps the books' (Psalm 58:1–11) in Part 3: The Rock Higher Than I

parts.title: Even When I Am Old
parts.epigraph: even when I am old and gray-haired, God, don’t forsake me
parts.lightName: Light of Even When I Am Old

paintings.title: preach to yourself
paintings.epigraph: “Why are you in despair, my soul?”
paintings.poem:
a deer at the dry creek bed,
nosing the stones
for water.

that's my soul,
the psalmist says.
thirsty for God.

and then he talks to himself:
why so downcast, soul?
hope in God.
I will praise him again.

sometimes you have to preach
to the only congregation
that's listening:
yourself.

paintings.title: two lamps
paintings.epigraph: “Oh, send out your light and your truth. Let them lead me.”
paintings.poem:
send out your light
and your truth—
like two guides
with lamps,

one on each side,
walking me home
up the hill
to your house.

light without truth
flatters.
truth without light
frightens.

send both.

paintings.title: wake up
paintings.epigraph: “Wake up! Why do you sleep, Lord?”
paintings.poem:
we didn't forget you.
we didn't turn away.
and still—
this.

wake up, Lord.
why are you sleeping?

it sounds almost rude.
it's in the Bible.

on a boat in a storm,
the disciples prayed it too,
and he stood up
and spoke to the wind.

paintings.title: a love song
paintings.epigraph: “My heart overflows with a noble theme.”
paintings.poem:
a wedding song for a king.

the poet's heart
bubbling over,
his tongue
as quick as a scribe's pen.

the church has always heard
another wedding
underneath this one:

the King
and his bride,
and a love song
that hasn't ended.

paintings.title: be still
paintings.epigraph: “Be still, and know that I am God.”
paintings.poem:
the earth shifts.
mountains slide into the sea.
waters roar.
nations rage.

and in the middle of all that noise,
a very present help:

be still,
and know
that I am God.

not a suggestion
to relax.
a command
to stop fighting him,
and let him
be God.

paintings.title: all you nations
paintings.epigraph: “Oh clap your hands, all you nations.”
paintings.poem:
all you nations.
not just Israel.
everyone.

clap your hands.
shout.

God isn't
a local god
of one small hill country.

he's king
of all the earth,
and the whole earth
is invited.

paintings.title: count her towers
paintings.epigraph: “We have thought about your loving kindness, God, in the middle of your temple.”
paintings.poem:
walk around the city,
the psalm says.
count her towers.
look at her walls.

then tell the next generation:

this God
is our God
forever—

he will guide us
all the way to the end.

paintings.title: nothing
paintings.epigraph: “for when he dies he will carry nothing away.”
paintings.poem:
the rich man's name on his land.
his house built to last for generations.
his gold.

and the psalm
shrugs:

he'll carry nothing away.

not one coin.
not one acre.

but God
will redeem my soul
from the grave.

invest there.

paintings.title: a thousand hills
paintings.epigraph: “the livestock on a thousand hills.”
paintings.poem:
God doesn't need your bull,
the psalm says.

every animal in the forest is his.
the cattle on a thousand hills.
if he were hungry,
he wouldn't tell you.

what he wants
is thanks,
and your call
on the day of trouble.

the owner of everything
wants
your company.

paintings.title: create
paintings.epigraph: “The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit.”
paintings.poem:
David wrote this
after Nathan's words found him out.

no excuses.
no spin.

against you
I have sinned.
wash me.
create in me
a clean heart.

not repair.
create—
the word from Genesis,
the thing only God can do.

and what does he want?
not the perfect offering.
a broken heart,
and he won't despise it.

paintings.title: an olive tree
paintings.epigraph: “But as for me, I am like a green olive tree in God’s house.”
paintings.poem:
the powerful man
trusted his riches
and his sharp tongue,

and he was uprooted.

but I—
an olive tree
growing in God's courtyard,

green,
rooted,
trusting his love
forever.

olive trees
can outlive centuries.
so do the planted.

paintings.title: the fool
paintings.epigraph: “The fool has said in his heart, “There is no God.””
paintings.poem:
this psalm appears twice
in the Bible:
as Psalm 14,
and here.

maybe because
we need it twice.

the fool
doesn't say it out loud.
he says it in his heart:
no one's watching.
no one's there.

and the psalm ends
not in scorn
but in longing:

oh, that salvation would come
and bring us
all home.

paintings.title: behold
paintings.epigraph: “Behold, God is my helper.”
paintings.poem:
betrayed by people
who should have protected him,

David looks up
and says the simplest thing:

behold.
God is my helper.

look.
he's right here.

paintings.title: wings like a dove
paintings.epigraph: “Oh that I had wings like a dove! Then I would fly away, and be at rest.”
paintings.poem:
oh, for wings like a dove,
to fly away
and be at rest.

he'd been betrayed—
not by an enemy,
by a friend
he used to walk with to worship.

he can't fly away.
so he does the next best thing:

cast your burden on the Lord.
he'll carry you.

paintings.title: your bottle
paintings.epigraph: “Y ou put my tears into your container. Aren’t they in your book?”
paintings.poem:
you've kept count
of my wanderings.
you've put my tears
in your bottle.

not one wasted.
not one forgotten.

and the smallest,
bravest sentence:

when I am afraid,
I will trust in you.

not instead of fear.
when.

paintings.title: I will wake the dawn
paintings.epigraph: “I will wake up the dawn.”
paintings.poem:
hiding in a cave
from a king who wants him dead,

David picks up his harp
before the sun is up:

wake up, my soul.
wake up, harp.
I'll wake the dawn.

he doesn't wait for morning
to start singing.
he sings
the morning in.

paintings.title: someone keeps the books
paintings.epigraph: “Most certainly there is a God who judges the earth.”
paintings.poem:
the judges were crooked.
the courts were bought.
the wicked prospered.

and the psalm is fierce,
the way the wronged
are fierce.

but its last line
is what the oppressed
most need to hear:

there is a God
who judges the earth.

somebody
is keeping
the books straight.

paintings.title: in the morning
paintings.epigraph: “I will sing aloud of your loving kindness in the morning.”
paintings.poem:
all night,
men watched the house,
waiting to kill him.

and David wrote:
but I will sing
of your strength—
in the morning.

the night belonged
to his enemies.
the morning
belonged to God.

paintings.title: the banner
paintings.epigraph: “You have given a banner to those who fear you”
paintings.poem:
after a defeat,
a banner.

not a white flag.
his.

lift it where everyone can see:
we don't win
by our strength.

through God
we'll do valiantly.

paintings.title: higher than I
paintings.epigraph: “Lead me to the rock that is higher than I.”
paintings.poem:
from the end of the earth,
when my heart is faint,
I call.

lead me to the rock
that is higher than I.

not a rock I can build.
not a height I can climb alone.

one higher than me,
and a hand
to lead me up.

paintings.title: pour it out
paintings.epigraph: “Pour out your heart before him.”
paintings.poem:
my soul waits in silence
for God alone.

not for the next news.
not for the right person to call back.
for God.

and meanwhile:
pour out your heart.
all of it.

he's a refuge.
he can take
whatever spills.

paintings.title: a dry land
paintings.epigraph: “My soul thirsts for you. My flesh longs for you, in a dry and weary land, where there is no water.”
paintings.poem:
in the wilderness,
no water,
nothing growing—

he doesn't pray for rain.
he prays for God.

my soul thirsts for you.

and at night,
on his bed,
he remembers,
and thinks of God
through the watches.

a desert
can be where you finally find out
what you're thirsty for.

paintings.title: one arrow
paintings.epigraph: “The righteous shall be glad in Yahweh, and shall take refuge in him.”
paintings.poem:
they sharpened their tongues
like swords,
aimed words like arrows,
shot from hiding.

and God
shot back
one arrow.

the attacks turned
on the attackers,

and the righteous,
once hiding,
are glad.

paintings.title: harvest hymn
paintings.epigraph: “Y ou crown the year with your bounty. Y our carts overflow with abundance.”
paintings.poem:
the river of God
is full of water.

he waters the furrows,
softens the ground with showers,
blesses the sprouts.

and at the end of the year,
the carts overflow,
the meadows wear flocks,
the valleys wear grain,
and they shout
and sing together.

harvest
is a hymn.

paintings.title: through
paintings.epigraph: “W e went through fire and through water, but you brought us to the place of abundance.”
paintings.poem:
through fire.
through water.

not around.
through.

and then:
you brought us out
to a place of abundance.

come and hear,
the psalmist says,
let me tell you
what he did for my soul.

testimony
is just this:
the fire was real,
the water was real,
and so was the way out.

paintings.title: the light on us
paintings.epigraph: “May God be merciful to us, bless us, and cause his face to shine on us.”
paintings.poem:
the old priestly blessing,
turned into a song:

bless us,
make your face shine on us—

and then the reason:

so your way
will be known
on the whole earth.

we're blessed
to be a blessing.
the light on us
is meant to spread.

paintings.title: an extra chair
paintings.epigraph: “God sets the lonely in families.”
paintings.poem:
father to the fatherless.
defender of widows.

and this:
God sets the lonely
in families.

not only by birth.
by adoption,
by church,
by an extra chair
at someone's table.

if you're lonely,
look for the table.
if you have a table,
look for the lonely.

paintings.title: up to my neck
paintings.epigraph: “Save me, God, for the waters have come up to my neck!”
paintings.poem:
the waters are up to my neck.
I'm sinking in mud.
no foothold.

it's one of the most desperate songs
in the book.

and it ends:
I will praise God's name
with a song.

not because the water went down first.
the praise
was how he kept
his head up.

paintings.title: hurry
paintings.epigraph: “Come to me quickly, God.”
paintings.poem:
one of the shortest cries in the book:
hurry.
God, hurry.
I'm poor.
I'm needy.
don't delay.

it isn't polite.
it's honest.

and it's in the Bible,
so you can pray it too.

paintings.title: old and gray
paintings.epigraph: “Don’t reject me in my old age. Don’t forsake me when my strength fails.”
paintings.poem:
you've been my hope
since I was young,
since before I was born.

and now I'm old.
gray.
my strength is failing.

don't leave me now—

not so I can rest,
so I can tell
the next generation
what you've done.

old age
isn't the end of the calling.
it's the part
where you pass it on.

paintings.title: like rain
paintings.epigraph: “He will come down like rain on the mown grass, as showers that water the earth.”
paintings.poem:
a prayer for the king:
may he be like rain
on the mown field—

gentle.
refreshing.
the kind of ruler
the poor are glad to see.

no king of Israel
quite lived up to it.

and then the book's last line:
the prayers of David,
son of Jesse,
are ended.

the church has always heard
another King
in this song,

the one who comes down
like rain.
